about.en:
NASA Space Apps Challenge is an international hackathon run by NASA's Earth Science Division with partner space agencies. Every October or November, teams in more than 150 cities spend one weekend building apps, data visualisations, hardware prototypes, games or stories that answer challenge statements written by NASA scientists, using NASA's open data.

The Zugdidi local event (hosted with Alte University) runs in person on 14-15 November 2026 at the Techno Park, Laghidze street 2, Zugdidi, in the Samegrelo region of western Georgia. It is open to coders, designers, writers, researchers and hardware builders aged 16 and up; no space background is needed. Teams of up to six people (four to six is recommended) work for two days with mentor guidance and receive certificates.

It is a low-cost way for school and university students in western Georgia to try a real international competition close to home: strong local projects can be nominated for NASA's global judging, and the format teaches rapid prototyping, teamwork and pitching in a single weekend.

en: Free, in person at Zugdidi Techno Park, 14-15 November 2026
Work on official NASA challenge statements with real open data
Teams of up to 6; mentors and certificates; route to NASA global nominations

eligibility.en: Anyone aged 16 or over, of any nationality, who can attend in Zugdidi. Students, professionals and beginners are welcome; no prior space or coding experience is required. Participants register individually and form or join a team (maximum 6).

en: Create a free account on the Space Apps website
Open the Zugdidi local event page and register for it (before 13 November 2026, 23:59)
Form or join a team of up to 6 people
Read the 2026 challenge statements, but do not start building before the hackathon begins
Attend both days at the Zugdidi Techno Park and submit your project at the end

costs.en: Free to participate. Travel to Zugdidi and accommodation are not covered.

score_reason: Free NASA-branded hackathon in two weeks with open registration; regional event, smaller than Tbilisi.

about.en:
The National School Olympiad (ეროვნული სასწავლო ოლიმპიადა) is the Georgian state's main academic competition for secondary-school students, administered by the National Assessment and Examinations Center (NAEC) under rules set by the Ministry of Education. Subjects are Georgian language and literature, Georgian as a second language (for non-Georgian-language schools), mathematics, history, geography, physics, chemistry, biology and foreign languages (English, German, French, Russian). Informatics runs in parallel through the separate GEOI olympiad.

It has three rounds. Round 1 is taken online from any computer during a set week in late November, with an optional practice test a few days before. Students who score at least 60% and rank in the top 1,000 in their subject go to round 2 (in January, at exam centres), and the best go on to the final round in March. In 2025-26 more than 19,600 students sat round 1, 7,800 reached round 2 and about 600 reached the final; 49 winners received diplomas and prizes from the Minister in October 2026, and winners could join the squads that represented Georgia at international olympiads.

The olympiad is free, recognised nationally and the standard first step towards Georgia's IMO, IPhO, IChO and IBO team selections, which the Rustaveli National Science Foundation runs in spring. Registration needs only the student's 11-digit Georgian personal number.

en: Official state olympiad in 9 subject areas, free of charge
Online first round from home, then rounds 2 and 3 at exam centres
Gateway to national-team selection for the international science olympiads

eligibility.en: Students at Georgian general-education schools (public or private) in grades 10-12 for each subject's age group; students at the basic level (lower grades) may also take part if they wish. Registration requires a Georgian personal ID number, so in practice it is open to students enrolled in Georgian schools.

en: Watch naec.ge for the 2026-27 registration announcement (expected early November 2026)

If you need special exam conditions, tick 'special conditions' and submit form N100 to NAEC or your regional education resource centre by the deadline
Take the optional online practice test, then sit round 1 online on your subject's day
If you qualify, print your invitation for round 2 and later the final round

costs.en: Free. Rounds 2 and 3 are held at NAEC exam centres around Georgia; travel there is at the student's cost.

score_reason: Free, official and the gateway to international olympiad teams, but 2026-27 dates are not yet published.

about.en:
GEOI is the national olympiad in informatics (competitive programming) for Georgian school students, organised by the Association for Supporting IT Education and Informatics Olympiads on behalf of the Ministry of Education, with the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation handling team-selection invitations. Contestants write and debug C++ programs (as at the IOI), and solutions are graded by an automatic testing system on the association's contest server.

It runs in two stages across three age groups (grades 7-8, 9-10 and 11-12): a remote online first round, then an in-person final in Tbilisi (two contest days for grades 11-12). First-stage winners need at least 50% of the maximum; final winners need 60% and a top-ten place. The top ten in each age group who score at least one third of the maximum are invited to two selection rounds; the best four form Georgia's IOI team and the next four are reserves. The national team then trains in Tbilisi in June and at a camp in Bakuriani in July.

For any student in Georgia who enjoys algorithms, this is the most direct route to international competition, and the past problems with full solutions and tests on geoi.ge are excellent free training material.

en: Free national programming contest in C++ with an automatic judge
Three age groups from grade 7; online first round
Top 4 represent Georgia at the International Olympiad in Informatics

eligibility.en: Students in grades 7-12 at public or private schools in Georgia in the current school year. Contestants must be able to program in C++.

en: Check geoi.ge from February 2027 for the registration notice

Solve the online first-round problems on the contest system
If you qualify, attend the final in Tbilisi; top finishers are invited to the IOI team selection rounds

costs.en: Free. Finalists travel to Tbilisi at their own cost; national-team training is organised by the Ministry.

score_reason: Free and prestigious route to the IOI, but the 2027 cycle is expected rather than announced.

about.en:
The International Scout Center Rustavi (ISCR) is a non-political, non-profit youth movement in Rustavi, Georgia's third-largest city about 25 km from Tbilisi. It runs a scout centre and social enterprise that gives children and teenagers a friendly space for non-formal education, outdoor activities, citizenship and sport.

Volunteers join this European Solidarity Corps project for at least four months, with entirely flexible start dates until the end of May 2027. They help design and run youth activities and support the centre's social enterprise. Five volunteers share a renovated flat 5-10 minutes from the town centre, each with their own room, and receive money for food. The Dutch coordinating organisation Eastpackers runs an intake meeting and preparation day in the Netherlands (travel to it paid) and helps with the motivation letter and CV; in Georgia volunteers attend the National Agency's on-arrival and mid-term trainings and have a mentor.

This specific placement is only for legal residents of the Netherlands; volunteers from elsewhere should look for ESC projects in Georgia coordinated from their own country. It is a fully funded way to spend several months living in Georgia, learning youth-work methods and earning a Youthpass certificate.

en: Fully funded: travel, housing, food money and insurance under ESC rules
Flexible start, minimum 4 months, until May 2027
Youth work with a scouting NGO near Tbilisi; Youthpass certificate

eligibility.en: Aged 18-30, legal resident of the Netherlands, available for at least four months, and no previous long-term (over 2 months) ESC volunteering. Must not be doing it to meet a study-programme obligation. Registration in the European Solidarity Corps portal is required.

about.en:
The Mtskheta-Mtianeti Regional Hub (MMRH) is a Georgian NGO based in the Tserovani settlement, a village built for people displaced from the South Ossetia region, about 30 minutes from Tbilisi. It works on peacebuilding, support for internally displaced persons and Ukrainian refugees, women's and youth empowerment and social enterprise.

The volunteer will strengthen the visibility and financial sustainability of organisations supporting displaced communities: designing a communication strategy, managing social media, creating content about the hub's work and the needs of IDP communities, running fundraising campaigns, developing newsletters and press materials, and reporting on performance. The deployment is nine months, starting around 1 December 2026, with an induction on arrival, capacity-building activities and field visits.

The volunteer lives in a house in Tserovani within walking distance of the office, with their own lockable room. Under the European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid strand, travel, accommodation, insurance and a monthly allowance are covered. It suits graduates or students with communications, marketing or fundraising experience who want hands-on humanitarian work in the South Caucasus.

Communications, social media and fundraising for IDP support
Induction training, field visits and own room in Tserovani

about.en:
The Mtskheta-Mtianeti Regional Hub (MMRH) works with internally displaced communities in the Tserovani settlement near Mtskheta, about 30 minutes from Tbilisi, on peacebuilding, livelihoods and youth and women's empowerment.

The Entrepreneurship Trainer designs and facilitates practical workshops on business planning, financial literacy and small-enterprise management; helps participants turn ideas into viable business plans and find microfinance or grants; encourages women and youth to lead small enterprises; and monitors progress. The deployment lasts nine months from around 1 December 2026, starting with a full induction and including capacity-building activities and field visits.

The volunteer lives in Tserovani with their own lockable room. Travel, accommodation, insurance and a monthly allowance are covered under the European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid strand. It suits business, economics or development graduates who want field experience in economic empowerment in the South Caucasus.

Induction, field visits and capacity-building included

No more than 3 months of previous ESC/EVS/EU volunteering. Background or strong interest in entrepreneurship, business development or economics; training or mentoring experience is an advantage. CV required.

about.en:
International Black Sea University (IBSU), a private university on the edge of Tbilisi, runs a series of free trainings for secondary-school students. Its 'UN Model: Peace Negotiation Simulation' is a fully funded project in which participants each represent a state or another actor and negotiate in an international-crisis scenario, aiming for a peaceful settlement and a joint agreement.

The format is a two-day intensive simulation for a limited group of pupils in grades 10, 11 and 12. It is designed to build critical thinking, negotiation and leadership skills in an international setting, and every participant receives a certificate from the university. Sessions are run in Georgian by IBSU's international relations and law faculty.

It is a good first taste of Model UN for students who have not yet been to a full conference, and adds a university-issued certificate to a CV or university application.

Two-day crisis negotiation simulation in UN style
Certificate for every participant

Wait for IBSU to confirm your place and the session dates by email or phone

about.en:
Ilia State University's Centre for Personal and Professional Development runs this A1 (beginner) course in Georgian as a foreign language for people who want to start from zero and adapt more easily to life in a Georgian-speaking environment. Teaching is based on modern conversational practice with many interactive activities.

The course covers everyday speaking (key phrases and expressions), reading and writing at beginner level (the Georgian alphabet, word order, understanding and writing simple texts), interactive practice through dialogues and role-plays, and cultural adaptation to Georgian daily life. It runs for 17 weeks (about 68 hours) from 26 November 2026: Mondays at 18:30 in person at the university with Professor Maia Damenia, an experienced teacher and textbook author in Georgian as a foreign language, and Thursdays at 18:30 online on Zoom with Maka Nozadze.

For international students coming to Tbilisi on exchange or for a degree, learning the alphabet and basic conversation early makes daily life, part-time work and friendships much easier, and a university-run course is more structured than apps or informal lessons.

about.en:
TSU Children's University is Tbilisi State University's long-running outreach programme (since 2007/08) that offers free educational projects to pupils from any public or private school. 'Literary Odyssey' is its new book club for teenagers aged 12 to 17, designed to develop critical thinking, close reading and a culture of discussion.

In the first season members read and discuss William Golding's Lord of the Flies, Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird, Jemal Karchkhadze's Antonio and David, Erich Maria Remarque's Three Comrades, Rabelais's Gargantua and Pantagruel and Ray Bradbury's Fahrenheit 451. Participants get three weeks to read each book, then meet at TSU for a group discussion of the author's intentions, characters' psychology and hidden symbols. The first meeting is on Wednesday 4 November 2026 at 16:00.

Selection is based on a short written task inside the registration form ('The main message of my favourite book'). It is a free, university-hosted way for literature-loving teens in Tbilisi to sharpen analytical writing and discussion skills that matter for essays and university applications.

about.en:
The European Solidarity Corps (ESC) is the EU programme that funds young people aged 18-30 to volunteer for two weeks to twelve months on social, environmental and educational projects across Europe and neighbouring countries, with travel, accommodation, food, insurance and pocket money covered. Georgia is a partner country, so young Georgians can take part.

On 6 November 2026 at 16:00 the youth organisation Umbrella will hold an information meeting in room G106 at Ilia State University (G. Tsereteli exit 1-3, Tbilisi). It covers short-term and long-term projects, funding conditions, what opportunities exist, how projects select volunteers and how to prepare a strong application.

For students who have heard of ESC but do not know where to start, a live session with an organisation that sends volunteers is the fastest way to understand the process and ask questions before applying to placements on the European Youth Portal.

about.en:
IBSU's Public Speaking Championship is a free project for pupils in grades 10, 11 and 12 who want to improve communication and presentation skills. It is run by the university's School of Law and Public Governance, with the dean among the trainers.

The programme helps participants build confidence, convey ideas clearly and persuasively, and run a speech effectively. Students learn to prepare logically structured, engaging talks, practise speaking in front of an audience and managing body language, and work on realistic scenarios before competing in a championship.

Strong spoken presentation helps in debate, Model UN, interviews and university admissions, and this is a free, structured way to practise it with university lecturers.

about.en:
IBSU runs this free Mock Trial project for pupils in grades 11 and 12 who are interested in law and want practical experience of court proceedings.

Participants are introduced to the structure and stages of a trial, develop legal reasoning and critical thinking, practise legal argumentation and analysis of evidence, and then take part in a simulated court case under the guidance of IBSU law faculty.

For students considering law degrees in Georgia or abroad, it is a free, hands-on taste of legal practice that also builds the argument and public-speaking skills used in moot courts and debate.

Learn trial structure, evidence and legal argument
Take part in a simulated court case
